title: 420Explorer governance scope decision and atomic reconciliation
subject: governance view
authoritative_statement: Governance is descriptive ecosystem subject matter and is not a mandatory dedicated 420Explorer Genesis view.

decision_authority.authority: repository owner / 420 Integrated Genesis product authority
decision_authority.instruction: Proceed to EXP-0.3.8 and complete all tasks required to fully qualify the step.
decision_authority.application: The registered Resolution B path is applied because the dedicated Explorer Genesis profile is the specific required-view contract and no governance implementation path was established.

rationale: contracts/config/420explorer-genesis.json is the dedicated Explorer Genesis profile and enumerates the ten mandatory requiredViews.
No dedicated Explorer governance API/view or required-view implementation path exists in the qualified EXP-0.3.2 path set.
Resolution B reconciles the broader application-purpose wording to the dedicated profile without silently expanding mandatory Genesis scope.
The decision does not classify governance as optional or post-Genesis; it states that no dedicated governance view is required by Explorer Genesis.

application_purpose.final_value: Blocks, transactions, contracts, validators, assets, finality

acceptance_effects.note: EXP-0.3.8 resolves only the governance scope ambiguity; all remaining acceptance criteria and blockers retain their existing status.

completion_conditions: All authoritative scope sources agree that governance is not a mandatory dedicated Explorer Genesis view.
The active governance capability and scope-decision requirement are retired.
EXP-FIND-001 remains available as resolved non-blocking historical evidence.
AC-5 and AC-10 no longer list EXP-FIND-001 as a blocker.
All atomic reconciliation manifest files are internally consistent.
The EXP-0.3.8 verifier and every retained Explorer/Indexer/repository qualification gate pass on the exact same head.
scope_boundary: This step resolves the governance scope conflict only. It does not satisfy unrelated runtime, deployment, workflow, security, recovery, or final Genesis acceptance criteria.
